ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZWw02w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhC-GwQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 27, "title": "Suppress WRAM-sourced DMA/HDMA writes to $2181–$2183", "body": "## Problem

Forward DMA and HDMA payloads sourced from WRAM can still overwrite the WRAM port address through B-bus registers `$2181–$2183`. This can redirect subsequent `$2180` accesses.

At baseline `396d4f75eaa47452f819b161b1eb4ae830c142b4`, [`SystemBus::transfer`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/396d4f75eaa47452f819b161b1eb4ae830c142b4/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L431) suppresses WRAM-sourced writes only when the effective B register is `$2180`. Other destinations reach [`write_raw`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/396d4f75eaa47452f819b161b1eb4ae830c142b4/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L339), whose `$2181–$2183` handlers change the pointer.

This is the unfinished behavior identified by the latest assessment and explicitly deferred in [Issue #25’s specification record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/396d4f75eaa47452f819b161b1eb4ae830c142b4/docs/issue-25-validation.md#specification-prerequisite). It extends the completed `$2180` fix; the supplied context lists no open Issue duplicating it.

## Expected outcome

Forward general DMA, direct HDMA and indirect HDMA must discard writes to effective B registers `$2181–$2183` when the current A-bus payload source is WRAM. Preserve all 17 WRAM-pointer bits and consume the transfer normally.

Apply these semantics:

- WRAM sources are all addresses in banks `$7E/$7F`, plus `$0000–$1FFF` in banks `$00–$3F/$80–$BF`. Re-evaluate the actual source address for each payload byte.
- Resolve the effective B register as `$2100 | ((BBAD + mode_offset) & $FF)` before checking the restriction. Keep the existing `$2180` conflict suppression.
- Suppression must retain source reads, transfer slots, DMA address/count progression, HDMA payload/table progression, line accounting and termination. It must not abort a channel or skip its remaining bytes.
- For indirect HDMA, classify the payload address using the indirect bank and pointer. WRAM-resident descriptors and indirect-pointer bytes do not themselves make a ROM/SRAM payload conflicting.
- CPU writes and ROM/SRAM-sourced forward transfers remain legal. Legal `$2181` writes replace pointer bits 0–7; `$2182` replaces bits 8–15; `$2183` replaces bit 16 using data bit 0. Other pointer bits are preserved.

The hardware basis is [Anomie’s Register Doc, revision 1157](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), sections **2181–2183**, **43x0 DMAPx**, **43x1 BBADx**, and **DMA AND HDMA**. The repository’s existing specification record attributes ineffective WRAM-sourced address-register writes to **2181–2183**, and continued DMA/HDMA progression to the transfer algorithms. [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), **SNES Memory Work RAM Access**, **Overall Memory Map / System Area**, and **DMA and HDMA Channel Registers**, supplies the corroborating memory map and transfer-register semantics. Document the HDMA applicability derivation explicitly; the general WRAM-to-WRAM prohibition alone is insufficient evidence for address-register behavior.

## Context and reproduction

An isolated one-byte reproduction can reuse the original fixtures in [`machine/dma_tests.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/396d4f75eaa47452f819b161b1eb4ae830c142b4/crates/snes-core/src/machine/dma_tests.rs#L776):

1. Initialize the WRAM port pointer to `$12345` and source `$7E:0100` to `$5A`.
2. Configure forward mode-0 DMA, count 1, and independently select BBAD `$81`, `$82`, then `$83`, resetting the fixture between cases.
3. Trigger DMA and inspect pointer, memory sentinels and final channel state.

Expected: the pointer stays `$12345` in every case; A-address becomes `$0101`, A-bank stays `$7E`, count reaches zero and DMA completes. Static evaluation of the current handlers predicts pointers `$1235A`, `$15A45` and `$02345`, respectively. These predictions were not executed during planning.

Existing [unit coverage](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/396d4f75eaa47452f819b161b1eb4ae830c142b4/crates/snes-core/src/machine/dma_tests.rs#L788) tests `$2180` conflicts, boundaries, progression and complete HDMA tables. The [original CPU guest](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/396d4f75eaa47452f819b161b1eb4ae830c142b4/crates/snes-core/tests/dma_access.rs#L228) tests `$2180` suppression and a legal ROM control. Neither establishes the missing B-bus address-register suppression. Existing reverse A-bus `$2181` protection tests exercise a different restriction.

Scope is the shared forward payload-write restriction and focused regression coverage. Preserve the corrected `$4210–$421F` read contract from Issue #23. Reverse conflicts, electrical/open-bus values, unresolved `$4200–$420F` exclusions, startup/alignment, HDMA initialization/overhead and first-frame timing, same-channel contention and the complete interaction matrix remain outside this change. Retained timing assertions are emulator regression conventions, not new hardware-timing evidence.

Planning inspected only repository content and supplied context. External specification links were not fetched; their attribution above relies on the checked-in validation record. No tests were run during planning.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the shared forward suppression for `$2181–$2183`, retaining `$2180` behavior and ordinary CPU handlers. Record precise specification sections and the DMA-to-HDMA applicability derivation with short supporting excerpts. Correct any contradicted expectation rather than retaining an unsupported contract.
- [ ] Add original, independently expected vectors for each address register. Use payload values that would change the addressed pointer bits, including both bit-16 directions. Assert the complete pointer, unchanged WRAM sentinels, completed count, final source address/bank and transfer timing under the retained model. Demonstrate focused failures against unchanged baseline production code, followed by passes after implementation.
- [ ] Cover both full WRAM banks and mirror boundaries in `$00/$3F/$80/$BF`. Include literal non-WRAM controls at `$2000`, ROM controls in `$40/$C0`, and mapped ROM/SRAM sources. For unmapped controls, assert routing/side effects without inventing electrical data values.
- [ ] Exercise fixed, incrementing and decrementing DMA sources, entry/exit at the mirrored-WRAM boundary, and 16-bit address wrap without bank carry. Check effective B addresses across all eight mode patterns, including mode 4 spanning `$2180–$2183`, a mixed legal/conflicting sequence such as mode 4 at `$217F`, and a BBAD-wrap control. Preserve the existing zero-count/65,536-slot regression.
- [ ] Exercise complete direct and indirect HDMA tables through repeated rows, a non-repeated interval and zero termination. Cover each address register, check table/indirect pointers, line state and active masks, and include WRAM-table/ROM-payload and ROM-table/WRAM-payload controls. Keep descriptor and indirect-pointer fetching legal.
- [ ] Add original CPU-executed guest coverage in `tests/dma_access.rs`. Guest instructions must initialize sources, distinct sentinels and the pointer, trigger conflicting transfers for all three registers, and observe pointer preservation through `$2180` reads or writes. Include legal CPU and ROM-sourced address-register controls, numeric WRAM results, a success marker, and explicit instruction/frame deadlines. Host code must not inject private state or expected results. Extend the MIT source/data/build provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`; acquire no commercial ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Preserve existing `$2180`, A-bus restriction, status acknowledgement, queued/deferred NMI, access-boundary, refresh and HDMA-preemption regressions. Pass these Rust gates from the repository root:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --lib machine::dma_tests
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dma_access
```

- [ ] Pass the existing original-fixture and licensed source-built CPU/SPC/HDMA gates, preserving source pins, assertions and licensing decisions:

```sh
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
  --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
  --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
  --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
```

- [ ] Pass the mandatory browser regressions documented in [README](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/396d4f75eaa47452f819b161b1eb4ae830c142b4/README.md#validate), using the documented prerequisites/compiler selection:

```sh
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

Preserve reproducible Castle/Memory hashes, all 18 existing browser checks, 18,100-frame game runs, Castle route completion, Memory win/restart behavior, audio checks and negative controls. Use the documented alternate test port if necessary. Do not shorten runs or weaken assertions.

- [ ] Update README and a focused validation record with actual baseline/final results, provenance, skipped checks and remaining uncertainty. Preserve all 24 inventory categories and their existing scopes/statuses; DMA and HDMA remain partial. Passing these bounded checks establishes neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
